texts.preamble: Syed Abdul Masi vs The State Of Telangana on 1 September, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana Writ Petition No.17657 Of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: 2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of habeas corpus directing the respondents to produce the detenue viz.,, Syeda Uzma Fathima W/o Mohd. Ali, now detained in Central Prison, Chanchalguda, Hyderabad, and to order her release forthwith by setting aside the detention order dated 03.06.2023 passed by respondent No.4 and the consequential approval order dated 08.06.2023 passed by respondent No.3 vide G.O.Rt.No.833 declaring them as illegal. 3. Respondent No.4 passed the detention order dated 03.06.2023 against the detenue under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, KL,J & SKS,J Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), under the category of 'Dacoit' as defined under Section - 2 (c) of the Act No.1 of 1986. 4. The impugned detention order was passed by respondent No.4 - detaining authority relying on the following two (02) crimes: Crime No. Offences Allegations leveled Remarks 32/23 of Musheerabad Sections - The detenue along with her Conditional PS 395, 419 & associates trapped the bail was 387 IPC and complainant (honey-trap) granted. Sec.25 (1A) under the guise of dating and of the Arms looted an amount of Charge sheet Act Rs.5,05,000/- from him. was filed (PRCNo.224/23) Syed Abdul Masi vs The State Of Telangana on 1 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29683246/ 1 6/23 of Santosh Nagar Section - 395 The detenue along with her Conditional PS IPC associates trapped the bail was complainant (honey-trap) granted. under the guise of giving Charge sheet catering order and looted an was filed amount of Rs.47,000/- from (PRCNo.215/23) him. 5. Crime No.32 of 2023 was registered by Musheerabad Police Station against the detenue for the offences punishable under Sections KL,J & SKS,J - 395, 419, 387 and 120B of IPC and Section - 25 (1) (A) of the Indian Arms Act. After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer laid the charge sheet and the same is pending for committal. The detenue is arraigned as accused No.5 in the said crime. 6. Crime No.6 of 2023 was registered by Santosh Nagar Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections - 395 and 384 read with 34 of IPC. On completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer laid the charge sheet and the same is pending for committal. In this crime also, the detenue is arraigned as accused No.5. 7. The detenue voluntarily confessed to have committed the aforesaid offences. Thus, with a view to prevent the detenue from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' respondent No.4 - detaining authority passed the impugned detention order dated 03.06.2023 and the same was approved by respondent No.3 vide G.O.Rt.No.833 of General Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department, dated 08.06.2023.
texts.arguments: Mr. Mohd. Aslam, learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the impugned detention order was issued without application of mind. The detaining authority did not consider the material properly. Therefore, there is no subjective satisfaction by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order. Thus, the detention order and the consequential approval order are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 8. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenue are serious and dangerous KL,J & SKS,J in nature and she is a habitual and dangerous offender involved in the above crimes. The detaining authority, considering the entire material available on record and after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only passed the detention order in order to prevent the detenue from committing similar offences and the same was approved by respondent No.3. There is no error in it. i) He has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. Union of India 1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh 2. 9. Perusal of detention order, dated 03.06.2023, passed by respondent No.4 would reveal that the detenue along with her associates target the business/vulnerable people, bait them and trap them by taking photographs (selfies) with the victims and blackmail them threatening the victims to make the photos public and also with dire consequences at the point of knives and extort money from Syed Abdul Masi vs The State Of Telangana on 1 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29683246/ 2 them to earn easy and illegal money to lead a lavish life. It is also mentioned that the aforesaid crimes would amply demonstrate the habitual nature of committing crime and creating large scale fear and panic among the people adversely affecting the maintenance of . 10. Section - 2 (c) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "dacoit" which means a person who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang commits or abets the commission of any of the KL,J & SKS,J offences punishable under sections 395 to 400 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. 11. 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. 13. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of . When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public Syed Abdul Masi vs The State Of Telangana on 1 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29683246/ 3 order are. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 5, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression . and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'.
